newsitem.title: UK: Little time for leisure on board British carrier.
newsitem.headline: Little time for leisure on board British carrier.

text.p: It's a rare occasion when Dean Molyneaux can sit back, kick off his shoes and take in a good game of soccer.
When you are the weapons engineer officer on an aircraft carrier, free time can be elusive.
Molyneaux is responsible for making sure the weapons work on the Illustrious, the fifth British Royal Navy ship to bear that name.

"The vast majority of my work (on patrol) tends to be in a crisis," Molyneaux told Reuters in an interview while the ship was docked in Singapore during a naval conference. "You don't get a great deal of free time."
Captain Tim Harris said the work day for most of the 1,000-strong crew, which includes 100 women, began at eight in the morning and would run for 10-12 hours.
He described work on the ship as "a 24-hour business". Overnight duty and weekend shifts were required to keep things running smoothly, he added.
"When the ship is at sea, it's pretty busy. We make the most of our time off and read books and that sort of thing. But it's basically a working environment," said Harris.
ILLUSTRIOUS INCREASING FIREPOWER WITH UPGRADES

The conventionally-powered Illustrious boasts weapons which include a squadron of six to eight Harrier jets, the vertical take-off and landing planes which provide the carrier with its main line of air defence, officers said.
There are seven Sea King anti-submarine helicopters aboard and one helicopter which can serve as an airborne early warning craft to track potentially hostile aircraft.
The Harriers and the Sea King helicopters will be upgraded before 2000 with more up-to-date models armed with greater firepower.
"With these aircraft embarked, we have much greater flexibility and punch," said a statement by warfare officer Lieutenant Commander Steve Entwistle.
Royal Navy officials said the eight generators on board would provide enough power to light up a small town.
The Illustrious has spent much of the last three years in the Adriatic Sea near Italy to support the various United Nations resolutions seeking to end the war in Bosnia.
Its role has changed since and the carrier has become something of a communications and command vessel for British warships in the Asia-Pacific region.
There are about 20 British warships deployed east of the Suez canal as the Royal Navy seeks to establish itself in an area dominated by the United States fleet.
"We want to be here with everybody else," Rear Admiral Sam Salt, the commander of the flotilla, told reporters. "This is an indication of our commitment to this area."
Molyneaux added: "We are the command vessel for all 20 of those."
The carrier, commissioned in June 1982, took part in recent exercises with the navies of Singapore, Malaysia, Australia and New Zealand.
The 20,600-tonne, 210-metre (690-ft) Illustrious is a pocket aircraft carrier compared to those of the U.S. Navy which use powerful catapults to launch aircraft and are about four times as long.
